name: Bean and Rice Enchilada Bake
summary: Tortillas layered with beans, rice, spiced tomato, and cheddar and baked. No rolling.
instructions: Cook the rice: 200 g rice with 400 mL water, simmered covered for 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Stir the tomatoes, cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, and salt together in a bowl. Mix the beans into the cooked rice.
Spread a third of the tomato mixture in a 9×13-inch dish. Cover with 4 tortillas (overlap and tear to fit), then half the bean-rice mix and a third of the cheese.
Repeat: 4 tortillas, the rest of the bean-rice mix, a third of the cheese. Top with the last of the tomato and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake 15 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more until bubbling. Cut into squares.

substitutions.substitute: 12 corn tortillas, layered the same way
substitutions.costNote: 12 corn tortillas cost $2.99 (La Burrita, Food Basics) against $2.15 for the flour, bringing the total to about $11.55

glutenFree.notes: Beans, rice, tomatoes, cheese, and spices are naturally gluten-free. Some corn tortillas are made on shared lines with wheat, so check the package if that matters to you.

budgetNotes: This is a big portion. It easily stretches to six servings with a side of shredded cabbage.
A jar of salsa can replace the canned tomatoes and spices, but it costs about $2 more and adds a lot of sodium.
Leftovers reheat well and freeze in squares.

pricingMetadata.notes: Flour tortillas No Name 10-pack (site estimate: 8 = $2.15). Black beans $1.50/540 mL (No Name). Rice $0.25/100 g. Diced tomatoes $2.00/796 mL. Cheddar $1.43/100 g (site estimate). Spices estimated.
